public_rationale: The claim is that Google, Amazon and Microsoft were bankrolling generative AI through big investments and through cheap compute for OpenAI. The record backs this. Microsoft put $10 billion into OpenAI in early 2023, and reporting based on The Information said OpenAI got Azure compute at a 'substantially reduced rate' (e1). Amazon finished a $4 billion investment in Anthropic in March 2024 (e2). Google committed $2 billion to Anthropic in October 2023 (e3). Microsoft's later filing confirmed $13 billion in commitments to OpenAI (e4, context). Zitron hedged the Anthropic subsidy with 'likely', so it is not scored.
limitations: The discount evidence is a secondhand news summary of private pricing, not a company disclosure.
I did not test whether 'subsidizing' means below cost. It is read as preferential pricing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google, Amazon and Microsoft are bankrolling the generative AI boom, including heavily subsidizing the compute rates OpenAI (and likely Anthropic) pay.

statement.excerpt: My last newsletter focused heavily on the ramifications of big tech — primarily Google, Amazon and Microsoft — bankrolling the generative AI boom, both through investment and by heavily subsidizing the rates that OpenAI (and likely Anthropic) pay to run their services, and through pouring billions of dollars of venture capital into AI companies.

from_speaker: big tech — primarily Google, Amazon and Microsoft
heavily subsidizing the rates that OpenAI (and likely Anthropic) pay to run their services
pouring billions of dollars of venture capital into AI companies
our_interpretation: Plain reading: by September 2024, Google, Amazon and Microsoft had put billions of dollars into leading generative AI companies, and OpenAI got its compute from Microsoft at preferential (below-market) rates.
Preferential or discounted pricing counts as 'subsidizing'. It does not have to be below Microsoft's own cost.
The Anthropic subsidy is hedged ('likely'), so it is not required for support. Big Tech investment in Anthropic still counts toward 'bankrolling' and 'venture capital'.
The claim describes an ongoing state as of the post. The target period covers the investments and pricing in place from early 2023 up to the post date. It is not narrowed to a single quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports or filings show multibillion-dollar investments by Microsoft, Amazon and/or Google in OpenAI or Anthropic during 2023–2024, plus reporting that OpenAI paid Microsoft discounted or below-market compute rates.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence shows the named firms had not made large investments in AI labs, or that OpenAI paid standard or above-market rates for its Microsoft compute.
